text: Hiring a car at Faro Airport is the easiest way to play golf in different parts of the Algarve. Book an **estate car** if there are two or three of you with golf bags, or a **people carrier** for a four-ball. Expect to need a **credit card** for the deposit unless you buy the rental company's own full cover. The main Algarve motorway, the A22, has been **toll-free since January 2025**. You can compare prices from the companies at Faro Airport on [EconomyBookings](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw).
Which car fits your golf bags?

Rental sites quote boot space in litres, but a golf bag is long and rigid, so the shape of the boot matters as much as its size. Estates usually take golf bags better than an SUV that looks bigger from the outside. This is a rough guide from Leading Courses, a tee-time booking site, based on published boot sizes:

text: Rental companies guarantee a car class, not a model ("or similar"), so leave yourself some margin. Stand bags are easier to fit than large cart bags, and laying the driver and woods loose on top of the bags often makes the difference. If you'd rather not fly with clubs at all, see our [golf club rental guide](/club-rental).
Picking up your car at Faro Airport
According to Faro Airport, the car rental desks are just outside the terminal: as you leave the baggage reclaim area, they are on the right. Six companies have desks there:

caption: Car rental desks at Faro Airport
note: Source: Faro Airport (ANA) car rental page, checked 17 November 2026. Check your pick-up time against these hours if your flight lands late.

text: Other companies, often the cheaper ones on comparison sites, are based outside the airport and take you there by shuttle bus. Centauro, for example, says its shuttle leaves from near the P4 car park, to the left as you come out of arrivals, every 10–15 minutes, and its Faro office is open from 07:00 to 23:00. Allow extra time for the shuttle, both when you arrive and when you return the car.
Deposits, credit cards and "no deposit" car hire

Faro Airport's own advice is that you need a credit card, because rental companies use it to hold a security deposit, and that some companies do not accept debit cards for the deposit. The deposit usually matches the **excess**: the most you would pay if the car is damaged. It is blocked on your card when you collect the car and released when you return it undamaged.

**"No deposit" usually means buying the rental company's own full cover.** Goldcar, for example, says its Super Relax cover removes the need to leave an excess deposit, and Centauro says that with its full cover you will not need to leave a deposit. Even then, some companies take a separate deposit for fuel: Goldcar charges for the tank of fuel at pick-up and refunds it when you bring the car back full.

If you buy a separate excess insurance policy instead, it can be much cheaper, but the rental company will still block the full deposit on your card. Goldcar's terms say so explicitly: with third-party insurance, the excess deposit is blocked and any damage is charged to it, and you then claim the money back from your insurer. Check the deposit and the accepted cards in the terms before you book, not at the desk.
Tolls: the A22 is free

The A22, the motorway that runs the length of the Algarve from Lagos to the Spanish border, has had **no tolls since 1 January 2025**, as confirmed by Infraestruturas de Portugal, the company that runs Portugal's roads. Some older guides still say otherwise.

By law, every rental car in Portugal has an electronic toll device, and companies charge a small daily fee for it: Sixt charges €2.23 a day up to €22.30, and Hertz €2.21 a day up to €22.14. Both say they refund the fee if no tolls are recorded during your rental. So if you only drive around the Algarve on the A22 and local roads, you may get it back. You will pay tolls if you drive further, for example on the A2 motorway towards Lisbon.
Driving between the golf courses

Most trips between the Algarve's golf areas use the A22, which runs a few kilometres inland, parallel to the coast. The old coast road, the N125, goes through the towns and is slower. Our guide to [where to stay in the Algarve for golf](/guide/where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf) shows how many courses are within 15 and 30 minutes of each base, and every course page on our map shows the drive time from Faro Airport.

text: Hire car or transfers?

Transfers make sense if you stay close to the courses you want to play. Once you play in different areas, a car can work out cheaper. As an example, here's a week based in Vilamoura with four rounds, using one transfer company's published one-way prices for up to four golfers:

If you'd still rather not drive, our guide to [golf transfers in the Algarve](/guide/algarve-golf-transfers-without-a-car) covers hotel shuttles, taxis and transfers, which you can also book on [GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA).
Before you drive away

**Photograph the car** all the way round, including the wheels and the windscreen, before you leave the car park, and make sure any damage is noted on the rental agreement. **Check the fuel policy:** with full-to-full, fill up near the airport before you return the car. **Don't pay twice for cover:** if you already have excess insurance, say no to the extra cover at the desk, but remember the deposit will be blocked. **Allow time for the return,** especially with an off-airport company and a shuttle to catch.
